_doc: Forge model routing = the GOAT router (: adopt the Model Routing Playbook by @donimas COMPLETELY and ALWAYS, as a HARD rule; supersedes the 2026-07-03 Opus-Lead / Haiku-trivial tiering). The Lead (main session) is the ROUTER on sonnet / effort medium: it never does the work itself, it triages (Head Chef), dispatches the owning Boss on the route's model + effort, has Verify Boss check every work package, and escalates ONCE on a FAIL. Route by ALIAS (sonnet/opus/fable) via the Agent-tool `model` param (overrides the Boss frontmatter `model:`); the route effort goes in the Agent-tool `effort` param (or a Workflow agent({agentType, model, effort})); a dispatch that passes neither runs at the Boss frontmatter `effort:` default (updated 2026-11-01: Claude Code 2.1.292 added the Agent-tool `effort` param, installed 2.1.316). NEVER set CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL or CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL (they flatten every per-agent model/effort). Forge logs the ACTUAL model used in FORGE_AGENT_LEDGER.md + the dashboard event 'agent_model_used' (registered 2026-08-01 in forge-dashboard/log-event.cjs + forge-bin/forge-verify.cjs + forge-dashboard/app.js), shaped {event_type:'agent_model_used', agent, model, source, note}. The model field is MANDATORY and must be null when the runtime model is genuinely not observable — a placeholder or guess is STRICT-REFUSED, so this event is never a claim about a model nobody checked. Never overrides governance, security, QA, or TOKEN_EFFICIENCY_GLOBAL_POLICY. Forge cannot auto-switch the session model; it may only recommend.
source: Model Routing Playbook by @donimas (famous-mandarin-287.notion.site, checked 2026-10-05). Global HARD MUST: ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md (GOAT model routing).
rules: 1. Tune effort before you touch models. Most tasks don't need high.
2. Don't default to the top model (fable). One tier below solves nearly as much for a fraction of the price.
3. Route by task type and risk with plain rules: triage -> quick | build | deep.
4. Verify with code (tests, types, lint). On FAIL escalate ONCE: more effort first, then a bigger model.
5. Log every miss and turn it into a rule (one-line lesson memory).
precedence: The routes below are the defaults. Risk wins over convenience: anything touching architecture, migrations, auth, payments, data, production or security, or anything unclear, is route 'deep' regardless of size. 'escalate' (fable) is never chosen up front. Haiku is not part of the standard: no route uses it.

lead.note: The main session is the router: /model sonnet (keep 1M context = sonnet[1m]), effort medium. It classifies via triage (Head Chef) and delegates; it does not do the build work itself. Changing the session model mid-task rebuilds the prompt cache, so the router stays on sonnet and the routes change per dispatch instead.

triage.when: FIRST for every coding task / work package. Read-mostly. Returns {"route":"quick|build|deep","risk":"low|medium|high","checks":["tests","typecheck","lint","review"]} and records it on the package's agent_work_package_created event.

quick.when: Small and well-specified, one or two files.

build.when: A normal feature or bug fix.

deep.when: Architecture, migrations, auth, payments, data, production, security, or anything unclear.

escalate.when: ONLY after a failed Verify Boss check on a deep-route package (one step up from deep) — never chosen up front.

verifier.when: After EVERY work package. Runs the triage checks scaled to risk (low = tests for the touched files; high = full suite + typecheck + lint + a careful diff read) and replies PASS/FAIL with evidence. NEVER edits.

codexReviewer.note: Codex is OFF (no account; the gpt-6-astra pin was refused). The codex-reviewer entry in agentDefaults below only says which model it runs on IF dispatched; the default flow never plans it. The switch is review.enabled in .claude/config/orchestration/codex-review.json (read via forge-codexreview-config.cjs isEnabled()); the review step falls back to ECC code-reviewer/security-reviewer, labelled FALLBACK.

agentDefaults._note: Default route per agent. Must equal the agent frontmatter model/effort == agent-model-map.json claudeTier/claudeEffort == agent-tool-policy.json model. Per dispatch the Lead may run any Boss on another route's model (Agent `model` param) — e.g. build-boss on 'quick' for a one-file fix. EFFORT HONESTY (updated 2026-11-01: Claude Code 2.1.292 added the Agent-tool `effort` param, installed 2.1.316): pass the route effort with the Agent `effort` param when it differs from the Boss default; a dispatch WITHOUT it runs at the Boss FRONTMATTER effort (build-boss on the quick model = sonnet/medium, a build-boss package triaged deep = opus/medium). Alternatives: a Workflow agent({agentType, model, effort}) or a Boss whose default route matches (boss/review-boss/security-boss for deep work). Always log the ACTUAL effort, never a route effort that was not passed.

processFailure.signal: Verify Boss FAIL because the worker skipped a file or did not run the tests.
processFailure.step: MORE EFFORT first: same Boss, effort one level up (low -> medium -> high -> xhigh) via Workflow agent({agentType, model, effort}); without a Workflow, the next route (quick -> build).

capabilityFailure.signal: Verify Boss FAIL although the worker had the full context.

escalation.secondFail: Stop. Report honestly to the owner with the evidence. No repair loop — failed cheap runs cost more than 4x a successful one.
escalation.afterEscalation: Append ONE line to the lessons file: '<YYYY-MM-DD> <task pattern> -> <route that worked>'.

lessons.writer: Head Chef (or the Lead on its behalf) after any escalation.
lessons.reader: Head Chef reads it before every triage; a matching lesson overrides the default route.

fable.use: ONLY as the 'escalate' route after a failed check. Never a default, never chosen up front, never the Lead.

agentToolFacts.modelParam: The Agent tool's `model` param OVERRIDES the agent frontmatter model. Forge passes the route model: sonnet, opus or fable (fable only as the escalate step). The alias haiku (Haiku 5.5) exists but is not a default route and Forge never routes to it.
agentToolFacts.effortParam: The Agent tool has an `effort` param (low|medium|high|xhigh|max) that OVERRIDES the agent frontmatter `effort:`, like `model` does. Without it, effort comes from the agent frontmatter, or from a Workflow agent({agentType, model, effort}) option. Updated 2026-11-01: Claude Code 2.1.292 added this param (verified in the installed 2.1.316 tool schema and the official changelog); the text before this date said effort could not be passed to the Agent tool.
agentToolFacts.unsupportedEffort: An effort the model does not support is silently lowered (xhigh/max -> high).
agentToolFacts.noGlobalPerModelEffort: Do not keep modelSettings.*.effortLevel overrides — they fight per-agent effort.
agentToolFacts.checkRouting: /tasks shows each running subagent's model and effort.

workflowAgent.scripts: .claude/workflows/forge-build.js (triage -> routed workers -> verifier -> at most one escalation) and .claude/workflows/forge-verify.js (read-only checks in parallel); structural test .claude/forge-bin/forge-workflows.test.cjs.
workflowAgent.documentedOptions: The Claude Code docs show agent(prompt, {schema, label, stallMs}); official plugin workflows also pass agentType, phase and effort.
workflowAgent.agentTypeEffort: agentType and effort/model opts: live probe 2026-10-06 (MODEL_ROUTING_GLOBAL_POLICY, wf_d46d1b07-6bb) showed frontmatter model+effort apply for an agentType and opts override them; not in the docs, so a re-probe on the current Claude Code is pending (owner-run, it needs a real Workflow run).
workflowAgent.concurrencyCap: The workflow runner runs at most 16 agents at once per run by default (CLAUDE_CODE_WORKFLOW_MAX_CONCURRENT_AGENTS); ultracode does not lift it. forge-verify batches checks by 16; forge-build caps parts at 4.
workflowAgent.ultracodeStart: Ultracode does not start workflows from -p, scheduled tasks or webhooks; a Workflow run needs an interactive session with dynamic workflows enabled.
workflowAgent.determinism: Workflow scripts are plain JavaScript without Node API, clock or randomness; a resumed run replays agent() calls whose prompt and options are unchanged (inferred from earlier owner workflow notes, not from the docs).

ultracodeDispatch.setting: ~/.claude/settings.json "ultracode": true (on by default for every session since 2026-10-06; also gateway/Discord-spawned claude runs; live-probed: works from --settings and settings files)
ultracodeDispatch.what: Standing dynamic-workflow orchestration: for every substantive task the Lead (router) authors a FRESH Workflow (often several in sequence: understand -> implement -> verify), one fresh-context agent() per part. NO fixed templates (owner rejected templates; the only bundled workflow is /deep-research). Quality patterns (adversarial verify, completeness critic, loop-until-dry, judge panel) are model-chosen guidance. Applies to every domain.
ultracodeDispatch.requires: dynamic workflows enabled (/config) and an xhigh-capable session model
ultracodeDispatch.preferredDispatch: Workflow agent({agentType:'<boss>', label:'<Boss Name> · <part>', model:<route model>, effort:<route effort>})
ultracodeDispatch.routedAgentRule: Every agent() gets its route via agentType of an agent whose frontmatter fixes model + effort (GOAT agents triage/quick/build/deep/escalate/verifier, Forge Bosses) or via explicit opts model + effort. Opts override the frontmatter: pass them when the route differs from the agent default (a Boss on a non-default route, the escalation step).
ultracodeDispatch.liveProbe: 2026-10-06, wf_d46d1b07-6bb: agentType 'quick' no opts -> sonnet/low (frontmatter applies); agentType 'quick' + effort 'high' -> high (opts override); opts model+effort -> applied; no agentType + no opts -> inherited the SESSION model (forbidden leak).
ultracodeDispatch.guard: ~/.claude/hooks/goat-workflow-guard.cjs (PreToolUse, matcher Workflow, timeout 10 s; has its own test file): checks VALUES, not just keys (F3) — a call passes with explicit opts carrying a real model (sonnet|opus|haiku|fable or a claude-* id) AND a real effort (low|medium|high|xhigh|max or an integer), as a literal or a const bound to one, with the goat('<route>') / GOAT.<route> helper, or with an agentType whose agent file declares both model (not inherit) and effort; undefined/null/empty, an unresolvable value, or a later key/spread that may override it counts as missing, and such an agent() is denied. Named workflows cannot be inspected and pass. Off: env GOAT_WORKFLOW_GUARD=off.
pipeline: worker part(s) (owning Boss, route model + effort)
ultracodeDispatch.costControl: Ultracode removes the built-in cost guards (hides the large-workflow warning, no concurrency limit for Agent-tool subagents, tells the model cost is no constraint). Keep the Dynamic workflow size guideline, the budget and the usage-guard pauses; triage + the low/medium routes are the cost control.
ultracodeDispatch.leadEffort: Claude Code 2.1.220: ultracode pins the Lead (router) to xhigh (still sonnet). From 2.1.284 ultracode is a separate toggle that keeps the chosen effort, so the Lead stays sonnet/medium (session.lead). Owner approved updating to the latest (v2.1.291) at the end of run forge-2026-10-06-model-routing-goat.
ultracodeDispatch.fallbackDispatch: Agent({subagent_type:'<boss>', model:<route model>}) with effort = Boss frontmatter — when ultracode or dynamic workflows are off
ultracodeDispatch.solo: Trivial or conversational turns stay solo (no workflow).
ultracodeDispatch.realAgentsOnly: agentType must be a real Boss/agent file; label starts with the registered Boss name.
ultracodeDispatch.switchOff: Remove "ultracode" from ~/.claude/settings.json (one session: claude --settings '{"ultracode":false}'); guard only: env GOAT_WORKFLOW_GUARD=off.

testGate.optOut: Set "enabled": false (or "mode": "off") in .claude/goat-gate.json, or env GOAT_GATE=off for one session. See config/orchestration/HOOKS_OPT_IN.md.

quotaHygiene: reference files by path (don't paste full content)
summarize logs to a path pointer
smallest team that fits (over-spawning is the #1 waste)
compact internal output; full only for deliverables
change effort before model; a model switch mid-task costs a prompt-cache miss
honesty: Log the ACTUAL model each subagent ran on (agent_model_used; null when not observable). Never claim a model, a verifier PASS or an escalation that did not happen. Never fabricate quota 'savings' numbers — real savings need real measurement (solve rate and cost per solved task, escalation rate, false passes).
